name: sync_d0_pair_then_hold
note: Three chunks 8 steps apart (L = 7): tce/acc invalid on the first chunk, valid from the second; boundary features held between deliveries; path_ineff/stall valid from t = 19 (20 trail samples); ext valid iff supplied (0, 2, then 4 values).

name: frozen_policy
note: All 15 rows equal the position: acm_neg = 0.0 (a frozen policy has the largest possible score), njr = 0 (0 / eps), reach = 0, speed_peak = 0; the second chunk gives tce = acc = 0. A motionless trail gives path_ineff = 1 - 0/eps = 1 and stall = 1 from t = 19.

name: dithering_trail
note: A single chunk, then a zig-zag trail (5 px/tick drift, +-12 px dither): over the 20-sample window the net displacement (~95 px) is a fifth of the path length (~466 px), so path_ineff (~0.80) dominates stall (~0.63); boundary features stay held.

name: sync_d7_overlap_absent
note: t_emit difference 15 == prev.horizon: the overlap is absent; tce/acc invalid.

name: sync_d5_overlap_l2
note: t_emit difference 13: L = 2, the degraded-but-valid minimum; tce/acc valid.

name: async_drop_d3
note: Async delivery with stitch = drop: the first chunk arrives at t = 3 with t_emit = 0, the second at t = 11 with t_emit = 8, so L = 7 (async keeps the overlap); a single ext scalar.

name: raw_prev_spike
note: The previous chunk carries a 250 px spike in row 10 (inside the overlap rows 8..14). features() stores the RAW chunk, so tce/acc at the second delivery see the spike.

name: projected_prev_spike
note: The same pair, but the first chunk is what the Tier-0 projection would have made of it (spike leashed to step_max). Its tce at the second delivery differs from raw_prev_spike: feeding features() a projected chunk would change the calibration/enforcement feature identity, which is why decide() passes the raw chunk.

name: short_horizon_h3
note: horizon 3 / exec 2: njr needs H >= 4 (invalid), acm_neg needs H >= 2 (valid); the second chunk 2 steps later overlaps by L = min(3 - 2, 3) = 1 -> tce/acc invalid.

name: dim3_pos2
note: Action dim 3 with a 2-D proprioceptive position: reach uses the first two coordinates; speed_peak's q_{-1} is the position for those and a_0 itself for the third (no step on row 0 there).
